decision: Use these model lines for any real decision?
have: 14 Week 10 lines built from 136 verified games, with published uncertainty bands.
lack: Out-of-sample proof of value. The model lost to a naive baseline (MAE 10.93 vs 10.62) and failed the gate.
recommendation: NO. Keep them as a transparency artifact and a baseline to beat, not as recommendations.

decision: Score the leaderboard on straight-up winners or against the spread?
have: Straight-up winner accuracy is measurable today (base rate 49.3% home picks).
lack: Against-the-spread accuracy: impossible without closing lines.
recommendation: Defer the choice until price data exists, but pre-register the metric now so it cannot be chosen after seeing results.

decision: Promote the 60.7% directional signal to the leaderboard?
have: 60.7% straight-up accuracy, 95% CI [52.6%, 68.9%], raw p=0.0156, stable across halves (59.0% early, 63.2% late).
lack: Significance after multiple-testing correction (Holm p=0.0626), positive Brier skill (-0.038), and any ATS evidence.
recommendation: Promote to a monitored watch-list only. Do not label it a proven edge.

decision: Price player props or prop combos?
have: Correlation structure measured; parlay maths published.
lack: Row-level official player usage and yardage data.
recommendation: NO for now. Blocked rather than estimated, to avoid fabricated distributions.

decision: Size same-game parlays as independent legs?
have: C2 margin vs total r=-0.161; C4 scoring vs opponent quality r=+0.386.
lack: A joint-probability model for 3+ legs and a larger sample.
recommendation: NO. Treat same-game legs as dependent and apply the correlation penalty before comparing with any payout.

have: Home win rate 49.6%, 95% CI [41.2%, 58.1%], fitted HFA slightly negative, n=135.
lack: Any multi-season baseline; one partial season is not enough to establish a stable HFA.
recommendation: Do not assume a positive home edge this season; re-estimate when more seasons are loaded.

decision: Claim we know the 2nd/3rd-string replacement chain?
have: Official Week 10 injury statuses and four official backup-QB situations.
lack: Official depth charts (NFL does not publish them; the URL returns 404) and participation data.
recommendation: NO. Report only what the sources assert; leave depth order blank and flagged.

have: A working scoring framework and published validation gates.
lack: A metric that passes validation, price data, prize terms, and legal/eligibility review.
recommendation: NO. Start with a zero-money paper leaderboard and revisit after one validated season.

have: Evidence that publishing failures is what makes the rest of the numbers credible.
lack: Nothing — this is a policy choice.
recommendation: YES, permanently. Every metric ships with sample size, CI and gate status.
